A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLM-FE research. All 21 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification and regression experiments, component ablations, feature-transfer results, HPO experiments, and noise-robustness analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds memorization evaluations, statistical tests, SHAP attribution, additional LLM configurations, and island-count experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the iteration endpoint from T-1 to T; the core program-generation, evaluation, and island-refinement procedure remains. Removal of ensembling is not established: v3 drops the explicit ensemble sentence in Section 4.3 but still refers to LLM-FE ensembling in Appendix B.2.

E1.justification: Section 5.4 adds five classification datasets for probing memorization: kidney-stones, health-insurance, pharyngitis, fico, and acs-income. The principal classification/regression benchmarks and Gaussian-noise scenarios are retained. This is a targeted extension of coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Base LLM and OCTree to the regression comparison, previously limited to Base, AutoFeat, OpenFE, and LLM-FE. The revised HPO comparison adds OpenFE, and the operator-frequency comparison adds CAAFE. OCTree's reported regression participation conflicts with the retained classification-only implementation statement in Appendix B.2.

E3.justification: Per-dataset regression reporting switches from N-RMSE to RMSE. HPO changes from 400 to 100 trials and adds MLP experiments with a 100-epoch maximum and early stopping. The documented in-context program count changes from two to three. New LLM backbones and a separate five-seed, five-fold statistical evaluation expand the settings. v3 also replaces convergence wording with a fixed 20-sample budget without early stopping; these reported changes do not establish that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds memorization tests, SHAP attribution analysis, and sensitivity to one, three, or five islands. It also reworks the HPO study and expands operator-complexity comparisons. Noise robustness, feature transfer, domain-knowledge examples, and evolutionary-refinement trajectories were already present in v2 and are largely retained.

E5.justification: Beyond the retained means and standard deviations over five splits, Appendix D.4 introduces one-tailed Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and significance reporting. These use 25 paired observations per dataset from five seeds across five-fold cross-validation. This is a separate statistical evaluation, not evidence that every existing result received additional runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for memorization datasets, three additional LLM backbones, revised HPO comparisons, significance tests, SHAP attribution, and island counts, while abridging detailed cross-model tables. Table 2 changes OpenFE's bank-marketing accuracy from 0.908 to 0.906 and LLM-FE's vehicle accuracy from 0.761 to 0.769, alongside uncertainty and rank changes. Regression results are replaced under different metrics and should not be interpreted as direct performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix Equation 4 corrects the Boltzmann denominator from a sum of scaled scores to a sum of exponentiated scaled scores, matching the existing main-text formula. Section 3.1 also replaces T = πθ(Xtrain) with prompt-conditioned sampling T ∼ πθ(p). No substantial new theory or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains LLM-guided evolutionary program search for feature engineering using domain knowledge, performance feedback, and memory. Claims of outperforming feature-engineering baselines and generalizing across prediction models already appear in v2; v3's revised abstract and contribution bullets retain that scope.

C2.justification: v3 develops new arguments that evolutionary refinement counteracts operator bias and filters memorization artifacts, and interprets SHAP and island-count evidence. The HPO discussion narrows its claim to gains over Base and OpenFE on three of five datasets. The Impact Statement adds substantive privacy mitigations, human oversight, and qualifications for safety-critical applications.

D1.justification: v3 supplies previously unspecified XGBoost and MLP HPO search spaces in Tables 7–8, along with MLP stopping and checkpoint details. Section 5.1 newly identifies four RTX8000 GPUs and defines which pipeline costs runtime includes. Baseline ensembling documentation is expanded, although implementation inconsistencies remain. The code/data repository is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds memorization literature by Carlini and Bordt, Qwen2.5 and Gemini2.5 reports, and an appendix elaborating distinctions from CAAFE and OCTree. Several optimization references are removed. The central positioning relative to evolutionary optimization and automated feature engineering remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites related-work and analysis passages, folds results and ablation sections into Experimental Setup, reorganizes generalizability and efficiency discussions, and restructures the appendices. The impact discussion is expanded and relocated, and publication headers and author formatting change.

P2.justification: v3 restructures regression and HPO tables and adds displays for memorization, search spaces, additional backbones, significance, attribution, and island counts. Efficiency and operator plots move into the main text; the operator plot gains a CAAFE series, and trajectory plots receive revised axes and layout. The document adopts TMLR formatting.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful comparative and diagnostic evidence, improves reproducibility documentation, and corrects Equation 4. However, its OCTree regression results contradict Appendix B.2, and Table 10 newly marks higher MLP RMSEs as better on housing and insurance, conflicting with its caption and interpretation. These unresolved reporting conflicts undermine confidence in parts of the expanded evidence, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
